result.summary: Independently re-ran test/scripts/test_parallel_tmpdir_cleanup_test.sh myself (not trusting TEST-DESIGNER's report) against both copies. POST-FIX (default target, this branch's scripts/test_parallel.sh): `PASS: clean exit, KEEP_LOGS unset -> tmp_dir removed` / `PASS: clean exit, KEEP_LOGS set -> tmp_dir preserved` / `PASS: failing exit, KEEP_LOGS unset -> tmp_dir preserved` / `PASS: failing exit, KEEP_LOGS set -> tmp_dir preserved` / `test_parallel_tmpdir_cleanup_test: 4 passed, 0 failed`, my own shell EXIT_CODE=0. PRE-FIX (`git show main:scripts/test_parallel.sh` saved to a temp file, pointed at via TEST_PARALLEL_SCRIPT): confirmed via `grep -c cleanup_tmp_dir`/`grep -c 'trap '` on that file both returned 0 (mechanism genuinely absent pre-fix, not a test artifact), then ran the test: `FAIL: could not extract cleanup_tmp_dir block from ... -- no 'cleanup_tmp_dir() {' start marker followed by a 'max_concurrent_creates=' end marker found (pre-fix script has no trap/cleanup mechanism at all)` / `test_parallel_tmpdir_cleanup_test: 0 passed, 1 failed`, my own shell EXIT_CODE=1. Fail-then-pass reproduced independently. Extraction technique verified genuine: ran the same awk extraction command myself directly against scripts/test_parallel.sh outside the test harness and confirmed the captured block (cleanup_tmp_dir() {...}, tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d ...), trap cleanup_tmp_dir EXIT, the following echo line) is byte-identical to the real script's lines 261-277 -- not a hand-duplicated copy. ISS-0699.yaml carries no literal acceptance_criteria field; the issue description's implied criteria (trap-based cleanup covering both success and failure exit paths, plus an opt-out env var for a run whose logs should be kept) map onto the handoff's own named 3 disposition cases -- clean-removes, clean+KEEP_LOGS-preserves, failing-preserves -- all 3 covered and passing in my own run (plus a 4th case, failing+KEEP_LOGS-set-preserves, proving failure-preservation is independent of the KEEP_LOGS check). No skip tags, no TODOs, no shared hardcoded state (each run_case uses its own fresh mktemp -d directory), no cross-test ordering dependency (each of the 4 run_case calls is self-contained), no secrets/connection strings in the test.
